A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CheXalign work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the additional material in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original preference-alignment experiments, report-generation results, and evaluations on six additional CXR tasks in Tables 3–5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds preference-subset CheXbert results and radiologist-annotated clinical case findings.

M1.justification: The four-candidate preference-generation procedure, GREEN/BERTScore Judges, alignment algorithms, model architectures, and LC-GREEN-guided configuration selection are unchanged. The new analyses do not modify training or inference.

E1.justification: Both versions use MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert Plus, and the same six auxiliary tasks involving RSNA, SIIM, OpenI, SLAKE, and Rad-Restruct. The added preference and clinical analyses use existing MIMIC-CXR coverage.

E2.justification: The existing comparisons retain DPO, LC-DPO, IPO, KTO, and ORPO, plus the same GPT-4V, MAIRA, Med-PaLM M, and LLaVA-Rad comparators. The new clinical examples use already evaluated SFT and aligned models.

E3.justification: V3 adds CheXbert evaluation of chosen/rejected training reports and a reader protocol involving one radiologist, three selected cases, and 18 reports assessed using reference reports and PNG images. Existing splits, training budgets, model sizes, and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 substantially extends the analyses with preference-quality checks using CheXbert and illustrated preference pairs in Appendix C.1, plus radiologist-led clinical error analysis in Sections 5.5/C.4. These add distinct evidence about preference quality, missed findings, incorrect statements, and residual repetitions beyond the retained analyses.

E5.justification: Table 4 gains explicit significance markers at the 10% level and an explanatory caption referencing the bootstrap intervals. Single-run reporting, 1,000 bootstrap samples, and the existing 90% confidence intervals are retained; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark scores remain unchanged. V3 adds preference-subset CheXbert scores in Table 9 and clinical case findings, and corrects misplaced CheXagent-2 statistics in Table 8—for example, chosen GREEN report length becomes 54.4 words instead of the incorrectly placed 0.24.

T1.justification: The LC-GREEN definition, DAA objectives in Tables 1 and 7, and RLHF/DPO derivation in Appendix A are mathematically unchanged.

C1.justification: The Introduction narrows the claim that preference fine-tuning had not been investigated in medical vision-language models to being sparsely investigated, acknowledging concurrent work. The abstract, five listed contributions, and conclusion otherwise retain their scientific claims.

C2.justification: V3 tentatively favors GREEN in the selected clinical cases and discusses unsupported temporal statements, unverified measurements, and errors missed by its annotation scheme. It also interprets preference-subset quality and qualifies the small reader study while adding concerns about biases in the data or Judge.

D1.justification: V3 supplies a specific CheXalign repository address where v2 only refers generically to the project codebase, and adds compute-provider acknowledgements. Appendix B's hardware, hyperparameters, sampling settings, and metric implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds Xiao et al. (2024) and Zhu et al. (2025) as concurrent medical preference-alignment work, Lambert et al. (2025) for the RLVR discussion, and a Marlowe compute citation. The lengthy Gemini author list is abbreviated without removing that cited work.

P1.justification: V3 adds qualitative-analysis and acknowledgements sections, expands Appendix C.1, makes localized language corrections, and replaces the individual-email author block with affiliations. The existing narrative and section sequence are largely retained.

P2.justification: V3 substantially expands the visual presentation with preference-example Figures 5–6, annotated clinical Figures 7–8, and Table 9. Figure 4 redisplays part of Figure 7. Original Figures 1–3 retain identical image content; table sizing, row ordering, significance annotations, and pagination also change.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly improves transparency through corrected Table 8 entries, explicit code access information, more accurate novelty positioning, and inspectable clinical examples. The gains are limited by the three selected cases and apparent averaging inconsistencies in new Table 9: the rejected CheXagent/BERTScore average is 0.419, although its four displayed F1 scores average 0.455. These issues weaken the added evidence, while the core benchmark conclusions remain unchanged.
